# Answer user questions hands-free for FAQ Bots in chat

**Pattern:** Chatbot Responder · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Chat

## Overview

Answers in a chat window, and covers faq-bots work end to end across Google Sheets, Slack and Notion.

It moves through 30 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. When Chat Message Received
2. Required Fields Present?
3. Abort — Malformed Input
4. Frame the Assignment
5. Coordinator Agent
6. OpenAI Chat Model
7. Research Specialist (Sub-workflow)
8. Draft Specialist (Sub-workflow)
9. Enforce Result Schema
10. Unpack Sections
11. Persist Deliverable to Notion
12. Load Previous Snapshot
13. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
14. Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
15. Record Sub-workflow Result
16. Enrich with Reference Data
17. Fold In Enrichment Fields
18. Fingerprint for Idempotency
19. Drop Already-Processed Items
20. Stamp Completion Time
21. Persist Run Metadata
22. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
23. Archive Row Snapshot
24. Guard Non-Empty message
25. Sort Conversations Newest First
26. Tag Pipeline Metadata
27. Stamp Processing Time
28. Summarize Run Stats
29. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
30. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing faq-bots work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

When Chat Message Received → Required Fields Present? → Abort — Malformed Input → Frame the Assignment → Coordinator Agent → OpenAI Chat Model → Research Specialist (Sub-workflow) → Draft Specialist (Sub-workflow) → Enforce Result Schema → Unpack Sections → Persist Deliverable to Notion → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow → Record Sub-workflow Result → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Guard Non-Empty message → Sort Conversations Newest First → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Stamp Processing Time → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Slack aligned by hand for faq bots
- Faq bots work that needs a judgement call per item before it reaches Google Sheets
- Faq-bots conversations in Google Sheets you would rather not staff around the clock
- Faq bots work where "Frame the Assignment" is still a manual step before Google Sheets

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Slack in step for faq bots, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Google Sheets or Slack are skipped, across all 33 nodes of this faq-bots build
- A failed Google Sheets or Slack call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 33 nodes in this faq-bots build
- Bad input stops the run for faq bots instead of landing in Google Sheets
- Every faq-bots run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Google Sheets

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Google OAuth2 / service account; Notion integration token; OpenAI API key; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

The Coordinator Agent never does the specialist work itself — each specialist is delegated to its own sub-workflow via a Workflow Tool, so every specialist stays single-responsibility and testable in isolation instead of one giant prompt trying to do everything. An output parser forces the final answer into JSON so downstream nodes can rely on the shape instead of parsing free text.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Add a third specialist tool and update the system message to explain when the agent should reach for it.
2. Loosen or tighten the JSON schema on the output parser and see how the agent's final answer shape changes.
3. Replace one placeholder Workflow Tool with a real n8n sub-workflow and measure the round-trip latency.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**OpenAI API key**
platform.openai.com → API keys → create new secret key.
_Gotcha:_ Needs billing set up; a brand-new key with no credit returns 429 immediately.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your faq bots process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole faq-bots payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.

### Conversation Memory

Carries the last few exchanges into **Coordinator Agent**, which is what makes a second question in the same session cheaper and sharper than restating the whole request.

In *Answer user questions hands-free for FAQ Bots (07604)* it sits behind **OpenAI Chat Model** alongside **Research Specialist (Sub-workflow)**, **Draft Specialist (Sub-workflow)**, so history and tools reach the model in the same call.

Feeds **Coordinator Agent** as `memory`

Window buffer, 10 turns deep and credential-free — move to Postgres Chat Memory if you need the transcript queryable later.
